cards.name: Adaptive Unsharp
cards.summary: Sharpen effect that accentuates edge detail by analysing the values of neighbouring pixels and sharpening adaptively, so edges get crisper while most of the image detail is kept. It has one control, Percentage (key Level, 1-100, default 50), for strength. How its adaptive analysis differs from plain Sharpen was not tested in this harvest; on the soft PGD photo even Level 100 changed nothing visible in a 1:1 crop (no photo pixel moved by more than 10 levels); only hard synthetic edges gained a one-pixel light / dark rim.
use_for: final crispening of a placed product or portrait photo before print export
restoring a little edge bite after a bitmap was resampled down for a layout
one-slider sharpening when you do not want to tune radius and threshold
avoid: noisy or JPEG-blocky images: sharpening lifts the noise too; use Unsharp Mask with a Threshold above 0, or a noise-removal effect first
truly out-of-focus or motion-blurred photos: it cannot restore focus, only add edge contrast
when you need control over halo width or which edges get sharpened: Unsharp Mask has Radius and Threshold
stacking several sharpen effects on one bitmap: halos and crunchy edges build up fast
the scripted path works only on a bitmap shape (Shape.Bitmap); convert vector objects to a bitmap first or apply from the menu

params.name: Level
params.does: strength of the adaptive sharpening (shown as Percentage in the dialog); higher values add more edge contrast
params.typical: 40-70 for print photos (default 50); 100 for the strongest effect

pairs_with: Effects > Adjust > Brightness/Contrast/Intensity first, sharpening last
Object > Convert to Bitmap on vector art before the scripted path
Unsharp Mask instead when the image is noisy and needs a Threshold

The command format is proven on 6 other effects; this effect's string was not applied in a harvest test. cards.name: Directional Sharpen
cards.summary: Sharpen effect that analyses pixels of similar colour shades to work out the direction in which to apply the most sharpening, so edges are crisped along their own direction. One Percentage control (0-100, default 50) sets the strength; how the direction analysis behaves on a given image, and whether smooth areas stay cleaner than with plain Sharpen, was not tested in this harvest. On the soft PGD photo Percentage 100 gave no visibly crisper edge even in a 1:1 crop (only hard synthetic edges gained a one-pixel rim), while plain Sharpen at Edge level 100 visibly crisped and roughened the same photo.
use_for: a one-slider edge sharpen when Sharpen's Edge level / Threshold or Unsharp Mask's three controls are more than you need
crisping architectural or text-in-photo edges after a resample
gentle edge definition on scanned artwork before tracing or print
avoid: when you need to set halo width or a noise threshold: use Unsharp Mask
badly blurred photos: it adds edge contrast, it does not recover focus
already-sharp images at high Percentage: edges start to look etched; keep it moderate
the scripted path works only on a bitmap shape (Shape.Bitmap); convert vector objects to a bitmap first or apply from the menu

params.name: Percentage
params.does: strength of the directional sharpening; higher values add more contrast along detected edges
params.typical: 30-60 for photos (default 50); 100 for the strongest effect

cards.name: High Pass
cards.summary: Removes the broad, low-frequency shading of an image and keeps only fine detail, edges and luminous areas, so the picture turns into a flat, greyish, slightly glowing relief where only outlines and highlights read. Radius sets how wide a neighbourhood counts as detail (bigger keeps more of the shapes); Percentage sets the strength (default 100 = full effect). Exactly how a lower Percentage mixes the original tones back in was not tested in this harvest.
use_for: a detail layer for sharpening: High Pass on a duplicate bitmap, blended over the original
an embossed, ghostly or etched look on a photo for a poster background
isolating edges before a threshold for a line-art or stencil version of a photo
avoid: as a one-step sharpen: on its own it flattens the image to grey; use Unsharp Mask or Sharpen if you just want a crisper photo
Radius at 1 on a soft or out-of-focus photo: expected to leave almost no detail, so the frame goes nearly uniform grey (not render-checked); raise Radius
noisy images: noise is high-frequency detail and is exactly what this keeps
the scripted path works only on a bitmap shape (Shape.Bitmap); convert vector objects to a bitmap first or apply from the menu

params.name: Percentage
params.does: strength of the high-pass effect; at 100 the low-frequency shading is removed as fully as the effect allows
params.typical: 100 (default) for the full grey relief; lower for a partial effect

params.name: Radius
params.does: size of the neighbourhood the effect compares against (1-20, default 1; unit not harvested): small keeps only the finest edges, larger keeps broader shapes and more of the picture
params.typical: 1-3 for a fine detail layer on a sharp image; 6-12 on soft images or for a visible relief

pairs_with: a duplicate of the same bitmap underneath, with the top (High Pass) copy blended through a Transparency merge mode for a sharpening / clarity layer
Effects > Transform > Threshold (or Effects > Adjust > Brightness/Contrast/Intensity) after it for a line-art or stencil look

cards.name: Sharpen
cards.summary: The basic sharpen: accentuates edges by raising the contrast between adjacent pixels, so the image looks crisper and, when pushed, crunchy with visible grain. Edge level sets the strength, Threshold sets how different neighbouring pixels must be before they are sharpened (0 = everything, including noise), and Preserve Colors keeps the original hues from shifting while sharpening (its exact behaviour was not tested here). An audit confirmed the EdgeLevel key changes the result and that scripted values above 100 clamp to 100.
use_for: quick overall crispening of a photo placed in a flyer or brochure
restoring snap to a bitmap after downsampling for a layout
sharpening only stronger edges (Threshold above 0) so skies and skin stay smooth
avoid: high Edge level with Threshold 0 on noisy or compressed images: noise and JPEG blocks get sharpened too; raise Threshold or use Unsharp Mask
when you need to control halo width: Unsharp Mask has a Radius
very blurred photos: it cannot recover focus, and heavy settings only add grain
the scripted path works only on a bitmap shape (Shape.Bitmap); convert vector objects to a bitmap first or apply from the menu
scripted values beyond the dialog range: stay inside Edge level 0-100 and Threshold 0-255 (410 was clamped to 100 in the audit)

params.name: EdgeLevel
params.does: strength of the sharpening (Edge level in the dialog, 0-100; unit not harvested); audit: EdgeLevel 15 vs 85 differed by 3.76, base vs 100 by 5.51, and 410 gave the same pixels as 100 (clamped)
params.typical: 20-40 for print photos (default 25); 80-100 for an obvious, crunchy result

params.name: Threshold
params.does: minimum difference between neighbouring pixels before they are sharpened; 0 sharpens everything, higher values leave smooth areas and fine noise alone
params.typical: 0 (default) on clean images; 5-20 on noisy photos or skin

params.name: PreserveColors
params.does: when on, sharpening is applied without shifting the original colours (avoids coloured fringes on edges); not tested in this harvest
params.typical: off (default); on when sharpening creates colour fringes

pairs_with: Effects > Adjust tonal and colour fixes before it, sharpening last
a noise-removal effect first on noisy scans
Object > Convert to Bitmap on vector art before the scripted path

cards.name: Unsharp Mask
cards.summary: Classic unsharp-mask sharpening: compares each pixel with a blurred copy and boosts the difference, giving edges a light and a dark rim that make the image read crisper. Percentage (1-500, logarithmic slider) sets the strength, Radius (1-20; unit not harvested) how wide those edge halos are, and Threshold (0-255) how different pixels must be before they are touched; it is the most controllable sharpen in the menu, and pushed hard it produces obvious glowing halos and boosted local contrast.
use_for: controlled print sharpening of photos in brochures, packaging and posters
local-contrast / clarity boost with a large Radius and modest Percentage
sharpening portraits with a Threshold so skin texture stays smooth while eyes and hair crisp up
avoid: large Radius with high Percentage when you want a natural result: thick white and dark halos appear around every edge
Threshold 0 on noisy images: grain gets sharpened; raise Threshold
badly blurred or motion-blurred photos: it adds edge contrast, it does not restore focus
the scripted path works only on a bitmap shape (Shape.Bitmap); convert vector objects to a bitmap first or apply from the menu

params.name: Percentage
params.does: strength of the sharpening (how much the edge contrast is boosted); the slider is logarithmic, so the low end changes finely
params.typical: 80-150 for print photos (default 100); 250-400 for an obvious halo look

params.name: Radius
params.does: width of the area around each edge that is affected (1-20, default 1; unit not harvested); small = fine detail, large = thick halos and a local-contrast boost
params.typical: 1-2 for detail sharpening on sharp images (default 1); 5-10 on soft images or for clarity

params.name: Threshold
params.does: minimum tonal difference between neighbouring pixels before they are sharpened; 0 sharpens everything, higher protects smooth areas and noise
params.typical: 0 (default) on clean images; 3-15 for portraits and noisy photos
